assumedContext: All figures are a look-through of IPTO at ADMIE Holding's 51% where stated.

findings.claim: The asset base is the strongest barrier to entry in this batch, stronger even than Constellation's nuclear fleet, because it is a legal monopoly rather than merely a physical one. Nobody may build a competing Greek transmission network at any price.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The RAB trajectory is specific: roughly EUR 3.3bn in 2025 to about EUR 7bn by 2029, funded by roughly EUR 6bn of capital expenditure over 2026-2029 and a EUR 1bn equity injection into IPTO.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE

findings.claim: The finding that materially qualifies the thesis. The Great Sea Interconnector — the Crete-Cyprus-Israel link, and the flagship 'massive interconnector project' — is a special purpose vehicle established by IPTO in January 2024 in which the French infrastructure investor Meridiam has become the MAJORITY shareholder. IPTO is the promoter; it is no longer the principal owner.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Great Sea Interconnector project company disclosures and Cypriot press

findings.claim: The consequence is that the largest single project in the thesis contributes far less to ADMIE Holding shareholders than the framing implies. A minority stake in a separately financed SPV, held through a 51% subsidiary, is a small fraction of a project whose headline cost runs to billions.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Part of that project is also not yet approved. An investment request for the Cyprus-Israel section was submitted to the Cypriot and Israeli regulators in August 2026, so a segment of the flagship link remains at the regulatory-application stage rather than under construction.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Cypriot press on the GSI investment request

findings.claim: The de-risking is genuine and cuts both ways. Selling down a technically difficult, geopolitically exposed deep-water interconnector across the eastern Mediterranean to a specialist infrastructure fund removes a large execution and financing risk from a company whose equity is valued for its safety.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The core domestic build is where the value actually sits and it is far less glamorous: island interconnections, the Crete link, network reinforcement to absorb renewable generation, and the substations and transformers that Greek solar and wind require to reach load.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the RAB plan composition

findings.claim: IPTO faces the same equipment bottleneck as PPC and from the same side of the trade. A EUR 6bn network programme is bought into transformer lead times of roughly 128 weeks and prices up about 77% since 2019. For a regulated operator the exposure is milder — cost overruns are typically added to the RAB and recovered — but schedule slippage delays the RAB growth on which the whole case rests.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived; cross-reference to the Siemens Energy dossier in this batch

risks.text: The flagship Great Sea Interconnector is majority-owned by Meridiam, so ADMIE Holding shareholders own a minority of an SPV through a 51% subsidiary — far less exposure than the thesis implies.
The Cyprus-Israel section was only submitted for regulatory investment approval in August 2026 and is not yet approved.
A EUR 6bn programme is being procured into 128-week transformer lead times; cost is usually recoverable through the RAB, but schedule slippage delays the RAB growth the case rests on.
The RAB composition by project is not disclosed here, so how much of the EUR 7bn target is domestic and regulated cannot be verified.

Annual RAB disclosure confirming progress toward EUR 7bn

conclusions: The asset base has the strongest barrier in this batch — stronger than Constellation's nuclear fleet, because it is a legal monopoly rather than merely a physical one. Nobody may build a competing Greek transmission network at any price.
The RAB trajectory is the entire investment case and it is specific: about EUR 3.3bn in 2025 to roughly EUR 7bn by 2029 on roughly EUR 6bn of capex plus a EUR 1bn equity injection.

The thesis's flagship project is the one shareholders own least of. The Great Sea Interconnector is an SPV in which Meridiam has become the majority shareholder; IPTO is the promoter, not the principal owner, and ADMIE Holding reaches it only through a 51% subsidiary.
Part of it is also not yet approved: the Cyprus-Israel section was submitted for regulatory investment approval only in August 2026.

That de-risking cuts both ways and is probably a good thing. Selling down a technically difficult, geopolitically exposed deep-water Mediterranean cable to a specialist infrastructure fund removes a large execution risk from an equity whose whole appeal is safety. The value sits in the unglamorous domestic build.
thesisImpact: Phase 2 confirms the RAB mechanism and relocates the value. The interconnector headline overstates what ADMIE Holding shareholders own; the domestic regulated build understates it. Phase 5 should value the look-through RAB and treat the GSI stake as a small separate item rather than as the story.
